title: Discovery and engineering of bispecific TCR-mimic antibodies targeting peptide–HLA complex
one_line: An end-to-end TCR-mimic discovery platform (pHLA immunogen, human transgenic mice, single B-cell plus phage, and proteome-wide X-Scan counter-screening) applied to WT1 RMFPNAPYL/HLA-A*0201, yielding CD3 bispecifics that kill WT1-positive tumor cells.
key_claims: From 12 transgenic mice, WT1-specific cells were 0.5–6.5% of IgG+ memory B cells, giving 95 hits/78 unique heavy-chain CDR3s, of which 11% (3 clonotypes) bound WT1 without mixed-peptide-pool binding; phage added 15 antibodies (2 clonotypes), for 26 total with SPR affinities 10^-7 to 10^-10 M and 25/26 non-binding to MAGE-A4 on the same allele.

Despite clean SPR, on T2 cells (100 nM antibody, 50 µM peptide pulse) 13/26 bound off-target M13L (RMFPTPPSL) and 14/26 bound PIGQ (RMFPGEVAL), with only 8/26 binding neither; comparators 33H9 and ESK1 bound both and 11D06 bound M13L.

X-Scan single-chain-trimer phage display of 172 nine-mer substitution variants resolved four footprint subsets: lead ATX-TCRm-06 depended on positions 3,4,6,7,8, other groups on four or three positions, while 11D06 and ESK1 tolerated substitutions broadly (ESK1 driven mainly by residue 1).
Proteome homology search from these footprints returned only the target peptide for the platform leads versus 4–12 candidate peptides for 11D06 and ESK1.

Knob-into-hole SP34 CD3 bispecific of TCRm-06 (KD 14.6 nM CD3, 35 nM pHLA) gave ~15,000 RLU Jurkat NFAT signal on WT1-pulsed T2 with M13L and no-peptide at baseline, and ~100% primary CD8 killing above 50 nM peptide pulse; a UCHT1/anti-HSA format of TCRm-01 and -06 killed endogenous WT1+/HLA-A2+ TF-1 and SET-2 with sub-nanomolar EC50s in two donors, with isotype bispecific not killing.
limitations: Authors state explicitly that direct cytotoxicity against a WT1-negative, HLA-A2-positive target in the primary CD8 T-cell killing assay was not performed and is ongoing work.
T2 pulsing at 50 µM peptide presents far more copies than endogenous presentation, so the off-target binding assay is a stringency test of unquantified physiological relevance.

The proteome off-target list is an algorithmic prediction from a mutational-tolerance motif using a proprietary internal method, not an experiment against the real presented peptidome; predicted hits were not synthesised and tested.

Benchmarking conditions disadvantaged comparators: ESK1 did not plateau at 100 nM so no EC50 was derived, and the authors hypothesise the single-chain-trimer linker interfered with benchmark binding in phage ELISA.
Lead monomeric IgG affinity (~0.1 nM) is not comparable to the monovalent Fab affinity in the bispecific (35 nM), so avidity loss on reformatting is unaddressed.
open_questions: Does a WT1-negative, HLA-A2-positive cell line survive the bispecific in the primary CD8 killing assay, given engagers can kill at occupancies below binding detection?
Do the algorithmically predicted proteome off-target peptides bind when synthesised and pulsed on T2 cells, as was done for M13L and PIGQ?
Would a head-to-head comparison under conditions not disadvantaging ESK1/11D06 support the claimed superiority of the platform leads?
